title: Dating apps suck. So I made a game over the last few weeks. 3 week project. Breakdowns inside.
author: Glittering-Chef-4914
selftext:
Took a break from my main side game projects to learn Astra and some workflows better.

**My experience:** About 15 years as only a 3d modeler in the game industry.

**Time for the project:** about 3 weeks of side work. I have a full time job and other IRL responsibilities, like my 300 reptiles lol. It still needs a lot of polish, I feel it's nowhere near done, but like the theme of the game, we should learn to love the not perfect stuff :)

I started with a general idea:

* I want to make a compatibility quiz that is not generic and useless like most are and in a format that would make people actually answer the damn question (picking skill trees and powers is how you show "this is who I am as a person"). Practical real world implications. I am currently re-writing the power ups to be more intentional about compatibility, the first pass is a little generic.
* I want to showcase who I am and what my interests are for someone to easily be able to see what is relatable as quick as possible because all our brains are fried by endless scrolling.
* I wanted to make the drain of dating more simple and fun. Ironically I probably overcomplicated the gameplay the more I went.
* I wanted 3 of my favorite game modes in bite sized chunks to try to figure out how to have a shared ecosystem in regards to my bigger game development projects.
* Characters can essentially be used within each game, because it's what I'm trying to do on my bigger main project, JKU - Jurassic Knights Universe.
* Aside from a general idea at the beginning, after that I simply thought of new ideas and features moment to moment of whatever felt cool and just freeballed it and put it in. There was no plan beyond the initial steps. I would have a random idea, try to stop myself from thinking about architecture and scalability and simply say "add this".

The trailer and breakdowns are from AI agents playing the game. 

You can play here:

[https://dateanthony.com](https://dateanthony.com)

# Setup

# ChatGPT Codex Astra

**$200 ChatGPT subscription - I hit limits frequently.**

My daily and main driver. I do the bulk of my work here.

* Stick to medium effort. Extra High just takes longer and doesn't change the quality much.
* Do not try to set up architectures and systems. Go off vibes and let it do its thing, then later you can refactor.
* It still  is not great at game development systems. It does not know how to make sprite sheets effectively unless you give it an exact workflow - my solution for this was to use blender to drive poses and use colors for positions of limbs.
* Once you have gold standards for things, you can reference them in the future so the AI has to follow them when creating new content.
* I tend to open many new chats and have several tasks working at once.

# Claude Code

**$100 subscription**

I use Claude for:

* Backend
* Refactors
* Optimization
* Analytics - I have 0 experience with analytics but I gamified these analytics and I will pick up some interesting data, like how long women are looking at which photos 😂

He's my engineer. I have no idea what I'm doing code wise, I understand fundamentals but I just say fix shit and it does it. I have been around a lot of developers so I know general processes and what is generally important. It loves to try and salvage work or make workarounds instead of actually deleting and recreating pipelines or code. **If anyone knows how to fix this, let me know!**

# Antigravity

**$100 Google subscription - Insanely generous, I don't even get closed to hitting limits.**

I use this for quick experiments or non project related apps.

For example, if I need to download MP3 files from websites, I'll just make a quick 2 minute app, walk pose workflows, etc. Anything I can think of that is tedious and I don't want to do, I just ask it to make a lightweight app for it.

I'm ADHD as fuck, so it helps break me away from getting bored on the main tasks because those side apps turn into mini apps.

I keep all of that in separate projects to not muddy the architecture of my main project.

In regards to how it contributes to my actual project, I use it for non-destructive, isolated content creation tasks:

* Audio generation
* Image generation, although Nano Banana 2 is very far behind now
* Stuff like that

Because it doesn't have the same type of long-form reasoning as the other agents, it's too dangerous to let loose on the entire repo. But it's fast AF!

# Web Tools

# ChatGPT Web Chat

**Included in the $200 ChatGPT subscription**

I do my brainstorming here:

* Drafts
* Game designs
* Storyboards
* UI mockups
* Random questions on what industry standards are to solve for X

I also chat here a lot so the context is not muddied by my project, and I can get better unbiased or brand new ideas that aren't locked into my existing project.

I set up a project folder that has sources for how to improve my prompts for each AI agent tool I use based on each agent's documentation. I'll give it a rough idea of what I want and ask it to improve the prompt for X AI agent. I make sure it still keeps it a relatively short prompt and doesn't over specify. AI agents seem to do better these days with less specification but more thorough intention.

# Google Flow

**Included in the $100 Google subscription**

I use it when I need massive amounts of experimentation for what things should look like, or when trying to bypass third party content filters by tricking it into big asset sheets.

# Midjourney

I use it for when I can't get past third party content blocks from other AI.

It does just fine generating pretty much any content, but it doesn't do a good job of matching an existing style, or at least I haven't spent the time to learn how to make it match better. I've only used it the last few days for a few splash screens.

# My Biggest Struggles

# Consistent UI

UI that doesn't feel like SaaS or website CSS Windows 98 bullshit. It took a lot of time and effort to create somewhat video game-esque UI without using textures. I still have to redo a lot of UI. It also felt impossible most of the time to have UI consistently reused or sharing the same styles. I constantly had to fight it going off course and for some reason I can't figure out how to utilize libraries as an architecture system; so re-using buttons, panels, etc.

# Consistent VFX

It loved to not follow gold standards of the initial VFX I was happy with. As the project grew and I had more approved VFX, it got better at matching them. I still need to redo a lot of VFX.

# SFX

Stable Audio 3 isn't the greatest, but it runs locally and is free. It tends to make Windows 98 magic like sounds and swooshes. I used QWEN for voice lines. Funny enough, Astra is really bad at directing it, but Antigravity is really good at directing it to make voices how you want them.

# Third Party Content Blocks

It's obviously a fan project with tons of IPs in it. I could trick AI about half the time, by trying to mix in several non third party content and overwhelm it. The other half of the time, I had to manually do workarounds to get third-party content working. About 50% of the project time was doing that by hand.

# What I will do differently

Not work on any of the project until i have the art style established at the beginning for the UI, with multiple UI breakdowns and demonstrations of multiple gameplay screens. I think Astra next time might have a better time being able to replicate UI if I give it consistent reference to hit. I'm currently working on a project that is a game development UI process for building modular UI from textures like typical video games workflows, 9 slices, etc.

Figure out a more consistent library system. It was very annoying to constantly pivot in how I review content. I say a lot "go off vibes" but I would really like proper architecture I just can't get AI to respect it because I'm not a programmer I don't know what it needs to do so.

Work on learning a seedance 2.5 workflow for cutscenes and things like that. I haven't used video generation yet pretty much.

# Questions

I'm glad to answer any questions. Ask away! Feedback is welcome, this is not final and obviously a lot of stuff is wrong, but I wanted to stop working in isolation and with my head down.

This post is all my own words, I only asked AI to format it and add capitalization. I know it sucks when devs just dump an AI generated post lol. I tend to answer every question so have at it.
